title: Capacity Garden: Operations Card + Burst Strategy Prototype
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, card-based operations control ('Capacity Garden' card) for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, short-term burst controls, and a predictive throttling slider. The card must be small enough to live in pool lists but expandable to reveal an inline micro-playbook with actions (canary toggle, drain, burst request) and readouts (heatwave score, burst budget remaining, recent SLO breaches). Goal: let SREs and product platform owners balance immediate response and cost predictability without leaving the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Card appears in Pool List and Pool Details with correct data mappings
Burst slider persists via API and updates pool policy (ENG API contract agreed)
Heatwave score is computed from the runtime metric set and matches the mock data in prototype
Canary toggle and 'Request Burst' action call stub endpoints (PRs linked) and show success/failure toasts
Controls obey RBAC: only Ops/Admin roles see throttle override and burst request
Design QA passes: color contrast, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader labels validated
design_notes: Visual metaphor: garden -> compact card with 'soil' sparkline for recent load and a 'budget flower' radial meter for burst budget
Use sparklines for 1h/6h latency trends; not raw GPU temperature to reduce noise for non-admins
Burst budget is shown as remaining tokens and a secondary numeric monthly allocation; requests above threshold open a confirmation modal with suggested mitigations
Predictive throttle slider maps to discrete policies (conservative / balanced / aggressive) rather than freeform percent to avoid accidental cost spikes
Trade-off: reduced on-card diagnostic detail to keep density; link to full Fleet Health page for deep debugging
Accessibility: chosen palette follows WCAG AA for color-blind safe palette; all interactive elements have aria-labels and focus states documented
Mobile: card collapses to single-line summary with an expand chevron; heavy controls hidden behind 'Manage' to keep list density
